title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: V is a 2-dimensional vector space over F2. Grothendieck writes V^* for the set of nonzero elements of V, not the dual; this is confirmed by 'Aut^-(V) = V'^*' and 'Aut^+(V) = W^*' read against 'V' = Aut^-(V) ∪ {0}'. So J = V^* is a 3-element set, and Γ := Aut(V) = GL_2(F2) ≅ S_J ≅ S_3 via its action on the nonzero vectors. Inside End(V) = M_2(F2), viewed as an Azumaya algebra, he splits Γ by the sign character into Aut^+ (the 3-cycles together with 1) and Aut^- (the three transpositions).

(1) V' := Aut^-(V) ∪ {0} is a 2-dimensional subspace. The three transvections [[1,1],[0,1]], [[1,0],[1,1]] and [[0,1],[1,0]] sum pairwise to the third. V' is canonically isomorphic to V by x ↦ τ_x, where τ_x is the transvection fixing x, i.e. the transposition of J fixing x. Any bijection between the nonzero vectors of two 2-dimensional F2-spaces is linear, so this map is linear.

(2) W := Aut^+(V) ∪ {0} = {0, 1, ρ, ρ²} = F2[ρ] is also a 2-dimensional subspace, because ρ² + ρ + 1 = 0. In fact W ≅ F4 as a subfield of M_2(F2).

(3) For the trace form Tr(xy) on End(V):
- V' ⊥ W, since the trace of a transposition is 0.
- On V' the form is alternating and nondegenerate: Tr(τ²) = Tr(1) = 0 and Tr(τ_x τ_y) = Tr(3-cycle) = 1, giving Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,0]].
- On W the form is the field trace form of F4/F2, which is non-alternating: Tr(ρ²) = Tr(ρ⁴) = 1 and Tr(ρ·ρ²) = 0, giving Gram matrix I in the basis ρ, ρ². It is nondegenerate, and F2·1 is an isotropic line equal to its own orthogonal in W.
- Hence M_2(F2) = V' ⊕ W orthogonally.

(4) As F2[Γ]-modules, with Γ acting by conjugation:
- V' ≅ V is irreducible.
- W is a non-split extension 0 → F2 → W → F2 → 0, with first map λ ↦ λ·1 and second map Tr. Γ acts on W ≅ F4 through S_3 → Z/2 = Gal(F4/F2), so W is the regular F2[Z/2]-module, which is indecomposable.

The next page notes that Ker(Tr) = V' + F2·1, the trace-zero matrices.

Purpose in the dossier: V plays the role of the 2-torsion E[2] of an elliptic curve, J its three nonzero points (Legendre/level-2 structures). He is recording the S_3-equivariant structure of End(E[2]) and its trace form, presumably for the level-2 analysis of moduli in the notes.
errors: No mathematical errors found; all claims check by direct computation in M_2(F2).

Minor: (1) is phrased as an iso with V via x ∈ V^*. This is consistent only if V^* means V∖{0}; with V^* read as the dual, the identification would go through V ≅ V^* via the unique symplectic form. Either way it is correct.

ideas.what: GL_2(F2) ≅ S_3 via permutation of the three nonzero vectors; even and odd parts plus 0 form 2-dimensional subspaces of M_2(F2)
ideas.modern_name: exceptional isomorphism GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3; decomposition M_2(F_2) = (transvections ∪ 0) ⊕ F_4

ideas.what: Trace form on M_2(F2): alternating on the transvection plane, non-alternating (the F4/F2 trace form) on F2[ρ], with orthogonal sum
ideas.modern_name: trace form of a quaternion/Azumaya algebra over F_2; trace form of F_4/F_2

ideas.what: S_3-module structure of End(V): irreducible 2-dimensional piece plus a non-split extension of F2 by F2 given by the trace
ideas.modern_name: modular representation theory of S_3 in characteristic 2 (Galois-module structure of F_4)

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, careful but entirely elementary computation of the S_3-equivariant structure of M_2(F_2) and its trace form, presumably as preparation for level-2 structures on elliptic curves. Nothing here would be new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: V^* (and V'^*, W^*) denotes the set of nonzero elements, not the dual space: J = V^* = V∖{0}, three elements; Aut^-(V) = V'^* = V'∖{0}; Aut^+(V) = W^* = W∖{0}.
'Aut(V)' underlined with Γ below means Γ := Aut(V), and Aut(V) ≅ S_J.
Item 1 reads: V' is a 2-dimensional subspace canonically isomorphic to V, associating to x ∈ V^* the transposition τ_x ∈ Aut^-(V).
Item 4 reads: V' as F2(Γ)-module is isomorphic to V and irreducible, while W is a non-split extension.
The 'NB F2.1 est son propre orthogonal' is a marginal note referring to W.
